root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence associates قنو vocabulary with retaining or acquiring something and with branched or elongated forms, such as a date bunch, spear shaft, or channel. It does not establish one uncontested abstract root principle.
root_idea.development: The Quranic قِنْوٌ denotes a date bunch. Related explanations connect قَنَاةٌ with قِنْوٌ through branching, line, and extension, while the acquisition vocabulary emphasizes keeping something as a permanent possession. These are reported lexical developments rather than a single meaning of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun, normalized to the singular dictionary citation form قِنْوٌ.

senses.definition: A cluster or bunch of dates borne by a palm.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form قِنْوَانٌ denotes such date clusters in the expression قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To preserve or retain one's sense of shame or modesty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with الحياء; the supplied evidence equates this use with اِسْتَحْيَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or acquire sheep or goats as a permanent possession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The possession is for keeping, not for sale or merchandise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gain, acquire, or take property and similar possessions for oneself permanently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of property, camels, and comparable possessions kept as permanent stock rather than merchandise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Livestock kept as a permanent possession rather than acquired for sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied evidence specifically mentions sheep or goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A protruding or aquiline shape of the nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related adjectival forms are أَقْنَى for a man and قَنْوَاءُ for a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spear shaft or hollow spear; also a pipe-like channel, conduit, or spout.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The channel, pipe, and spout applications belong to the same hollow, elongated semantic branch as the spear shaft.
This is a reported Classical sense, explicitly attributed as such and cross-referenced in the supplied evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An Egyptian regional name for وُشَّق, also called أُشَّق or أُشَّج.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional plant or substance name in the supplied lexical record.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most preservative, especially of modesty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the proverbial expression خَلَاؤُكَ أَقْنَى لِحَيَائِكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The weaving together of one white thread and one black thread.

cautions: The only QAC occurrence is the noun قِنْوَانٌ at 6:99:23; قِنْوٌ is used as the normalized singular citation form.
The wild-cow sense of قَنَاةٌ is included as a reported Classical usage, not as a Quranic sense.
